A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ZETA study and contain complete Appendices A-G. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison; the appendix pages are visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original ZETA experiments on MQAR, LRA and WikiText-103, efficiency benchmarks, and additional ablations in Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results, efficiency measurements and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2-3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same low-dimensional keys/queries, Z-order projection, chunked causal retrieval, adaptive Cauchy-Softmax and historical-mean smoothing. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MQAR, the same five LRA tasks, WikiText-103, and the same locality-preservation and efficiency scenarios. Appendix G retains its ListOps/Image and MQAR experiments.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Figure 2, Tables 1-4 and Appendix G. This includes the MQAR attention/Performer/BASED comparison and the efficiency comparison against Torch Attention, Mamba and Flash Attention.

E3.justification: The reported metrics, dimensionality sweeps, model sizes, benchmark sequence lengths and Appendix C configurations remain unchanged. Removing the hardware disclosure does not establish a change to the experiment itself.

E4.justification: Sections 4.2-4.5 retain the same dimensionality, similarity-operator, locality-preservation and top-k analyses. Appendix G's additional dimensionality and similarity-metric ablations are identical.

E5.justification: Both versions present the same point estimates and curves without reported experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Reported values and plotted results are unchanged, including ZETA's WikiText-103 perplexity of 26.3 in Table 1 and LRA average of 63.51 in Table 2. Efficiency Tables 3-4, Appendix Tables 5-6 and Figures 2-3 also retain their results.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.1, Assumption 3.2 and Theorem 3.3 retain the same mathematical content. Appendix A's proofs and Appendix E's gradient derivations are identical; equation reflow introduces no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about parallel top-k attention, O(N log N) complexity, dimensionality selection, adaptive Cauchy-Softmax and benchmark performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations of low-dimensional keys/queries, Cauchy kernels and efficiency-performance trade-offs remain unchanged. Appendix F retains the limitation that top-k selection can overlook important tokens with low attention scores.

D1.justification: Section 4.6 in v1 specifies benchmarking on a single NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU; v3 deletes this information without replacing it elsewhere. The implementation and configuration details in Appendices C-E remain unchanged. This is a loss of reproducibility information, not evidence of different hardware being used.

R1.justification: The introduction adds five works: Fang et al. (2022, 2025) and Zeng et al. (2023, 2024a, 2024b), with corresponding bibliography entries. The efficient-attention related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Vector Institute affiliations for Charles Ling and Boyu Wang, identifies Boyu Wang alone as corresponding author, and inserts citations in the opening paragraph. Scientific prose and section organization are largely retained, without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 5 to page 6. Tables 2-4 place captions above their contents, and Tables 3-4 become smaller. Other changes mainly involve spacing and pagination; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 removes the only identification of the benchmark GPU from Section 4.6, modestly weakening reproducibility and interpretation of the efficiency measurements in Tables 3-4. The added background citations and limited presentation edits provide no substantial compensating gain, while the scientific content and results remain unchanged.
